ai.description: This small toad reaches 3–4 cm. It is dark brown with irregular yellow-orange dorsal patches and a granular skin texture. Key features include a flattened body and prominent, enlarged parotoid glands.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Malabar Torrent Toad is best identified by the distinct, bright yellow or orange reticulated pattern covering its dark, granular skin, which contrasts with other toads.
ai.habitat: The Malabar Torrent Toad inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Malabar Torrent Toad is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours clinging to wet, mossy rocks near fast-flowing streams to hunt for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Malabar Torrent Toad breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of pigmented eggs in flowing mountain streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Malabar Torrent Toad is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, found in states like Kerala and Karnataka at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Torrent Toad emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic chirps, typically heard above the constant roar of fast-flowing mountain streams.
